successCriteria.description: The `Employee` interface is exported from `src/modules/employee/employee.model.ts` with all canonical fields: `id: string`, `employeeNumber: string`, `firstName: string`, `lastName: string`, `email: string`, `managerId: string | null`, `department: string | null`, `hireDate: Date`, `terminationDate: Date | null`, `employmentStatus: 'ACTIVE' | 'INACTIVE' | 'TERMINATED'`, `createdAt: Date`, `updatedAt: Date`, `deletedAt: Date | null`.

The `IEmployeeRepository` interface is exported from `src/modules/employee/employee.repository.ts` with methods: `findById(id: string): Promise<Employee | null>`, `findByEmployeeNumber(employeeNumber: string): Promise<Employee | null>`, `findAll(): Promise<Employee[]>`, `create(employee: Omit<Employee, 'id' | 'createdAt' | 'updatedAt' | 'deletedAt'>): Promise<Employee>`, `update(id: string, data: Partial<Employee>): Promise<Employee | null>`, `softDelete(id: string): Promise<void>`.
The `EmployeeRepository` class implements `IEmployeeRepository` and uses the `pool` from `src/shared/db/connection.ts` with parameterized SQL queries (no string concatenation of user input into SQL).

Jest unit tests exist in `tests/unit/modules/employee/` covering: (a) `EmployeeRepository.create` persists a row and returns it with generated `id`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`; (b) `findById` returns the employee or null; (c) `findByEmployeeNumber` returns the employee or null; (d) `findAll` returns all non-soft-deleted employees; (e) `update` modifies fields and returns the updated employee or null; (f) `softDelete` sets `deletedAt` and the employee is excluded from `findAll`/`findById` thereafter.

constraints: All database access must go through the repository pattern — no inline SQL in models, services, or barrel exports (GP-001).
The `EmployeeRepository` must use parameterized queries (`$1`, `$2`, …) via the `pg` `pool` — never string interpolation of user-supplied values into SQL.

The `Employee` interface must match the reconciled architecture entity shape exactly: `id: string`, `employeeNumber: string`, `firstName: string`, `lastName: string`, `email: string`, `managerId: string | null`, `department: string | null`, `hireDate: Date`, `terminationDate: Date | null`, `employmentStatus: 'ACTIVE' | 'INACTIVE' | 'TERMINATED'`, `createdAt: Date`, `updatedAt: Date`, `deletedAt: Date | null`.
